title: Ops: running commands safely with approval
when: The ops worker must run shell commands (start a server, run tests, copy files) in the user workspace, where each run may need approval.
prompt:
Goal: Commands that are read only first, scoped to the workspace, explained before they run, and never destructive without a backup and approval.
Steps:
1. Prefer tools over shell: list_files and read_file instead of ls and cat, check instead of ad hoc scripts.
2. Before each run, say in one line what it does and what it changes; the user approves with that text.
3. Start with a read only command (node --version, a dry run flag) before one that writes.
4. Scope every path inside the workspace with relative paths; never touch home, system or parent folders.
5. For anything that deletes or overwrites, make a copy first and name it in the approval text.
6. Read the output and exit code after each run; stop and report on a non zero exit instead of trying random fixes.
Quality bar:
- Every command has a stated purpose.
- No command reaches outside the workspace.
- Failures are reported with the output.
Pitfalls:
- Chaining many commands so one approval hides a risky one.
- Recursive deletes with wildcards.
- Commands that download or install anything.
Verify:
- [ ] Read only commands came first.
- [ ] Paths are relative.
- [ ] Backups precede destructive steps.
- [ ] Exit codes were checked.
Output: A note listing each command, why it ran and its result.

examples.input: roda os testes e sobe o servidor local
examples.output: say: "runs node test.mjs, writes nothing"; then "starts node server.mjs on port 3000"
